reason: Reproduced exactly, and the consequence is user-visible data loss, not a latent collision. render-b.js:1117 mints `id: "moment-" + (F.milestones.length + 1)` while the delete branch splices the array, so the counter runs backwards. Driven in chromium at 1440 on state=owner-flight: Add, Add, delete the first of the two, Add leaves F.milestones holding TWO records with id "moment-12" (dated 2026-07-18 and 2026-07-17). recordFor() (render-b.js:71) returns the first, and setTitle/setAway/commitDate/the delete branch all resolve through it, so every write from the NEW row lands on the OLD record. Named run: added "Ceremony rehearsal" (moment-11) and "Hair trial" (moment-12), deleted "Ceremony rehearsal", added a third and typed "Rehearsal dinner" - the records immediately read ["Rehearsal dinner"@07-18, blank@07-17] while the screen still read ["Rehearsal dinner", "Hair trial"]. The owner's "Hair trial" was destroyed with no console error and no visible sign. Previewing the guest view and returning remounted from the records and the screen then read ["Untitled moment"@07-17, "Rehearsal dinner"@07-18]: the named moment is gone and the two rows have swapped identity. A +7 press on the new row moved the OTHER record's date. Opening the top row afterwards gave a panel announcing aria-label "Editing Rehearsal dinner" for a row displaying "Untitled moment"; pressing Delete removed that row from the DOM but spliced the other record out, leaving the undo bar saying "Rehearsal dinner was removed." with a row reading "Rehearsal dinner" still on screen. Undo's focus restore at render-b.js:579 uses querySelector('.b-item[data-id="..."]'), which under a duplicate id lands on the wrong row. The shortest real path is shorter than the finding claims: round 9's new empty-project branch (render-b.js:1484) resets F.milestones to a single "moment-1", so a brand-new project reaches the collision in four owner actions - name the first moment, add a second ("Cake tasting", moment-2), delete the first, add a third. Records then read ["Order flowers"@08-18, blank@08-11] against a screen reading ["Order flowers", "Cake tasting"]. Not covered by either gate: interaction-check.mjs never performs add/delete/add and asserts nothing about id uniqueness; audit.mjs only sees the first render. Not in lessons.md, not in the settled list, and not the out-of-scope "data model" - it is a correctness defect in the reviewed renderer, fixed by one counter. At a 9.5 bar, silently overwriting a moment the owner named, on the flagship owner flow, is disqualifying.
sharpenedFix: Module-scoped monotonic counter in render-b.js beside `var history = [];`: `var minted = F.milestones.length;` and `id: "moment-" + (++minted)` in the add branch. Also reset it in the empty-project branch at render-b.js:1484 - alongside `F.milestones.length = 0;` and the `moment-1` push, set `minted = 1;` - so a fresh project reads moment-1, moment-2, moment-3 rather than jumping to moment-11, and the counter is still monotonic within that project's life. Neither can collide with the fixture's demo-audience-item-* ids. Add two assertions to interaction-check.mjs after an add/add/delete/add run: (1) the set of F.milestones ids contains no duplicates, and (2) after typing a name into the third moment's title field, recordFor() of the row that was typed into carries that name and no other record's title changed - assertion (2) is the one that would have caught this, since a uniqueness check alone would not have shown the write landing on the wrong record.
